definitions.explanation: Refers back to something that was mentioned or described earlier in a text or document.

examples.japanese: {前記|ぜんき}の{条件|じょうけん}に{同意|どうい}する。
examples.english: I agree to the aforementioned conditions.

examples.japanese: {前記|ぜんき}の{通|とお}り、{申|もう}し{込|こ}みは{来月|らいげつ}{末|まつ}までです。
examples.english: As stated above, the application deadline is the end of next month.

examples.japanese: {前記|ぜんき}の{内容|ないよう}に{誤|あやま}りがあれば、{速|すみ}やかにご{連絡|れんらく}ください。
examples.english: If there are any errors in the above content, please contact us promptly.

notes:
Composed of {前|ぜん} (before, previous) + {記|き} (record, write). A formal written term used in documents, contracts, articles, and official correspondence to refer back to something previously written.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {前記|ぜんき}の{通|とお}り — as stated above
- {前記|ぜんき}の{条件|じょうけん} — the aforementioned conditions
- {前記|ぜんき}の{内容|ないよう} — the above content
- {前記|ぜんき}の{事項|じこう} — the aforementioned matters

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {上記|じょうき} — above-mentioned (very similar; more commonly used in modern documents)
- {上述|じょうじゅつ} — aforementioned (more formal/academic)
- {下記|かき} — below-mentioned (the opposite: referring to what follows)
- {後述|こうじゅつ} — described later (formal; refers to what will be mentioned later)

REGISTER:
Strictly a written, formal term. Not used in conversation. In casual writing, {上|うえ}の or さっきの would be used instead.
